who: a husband and wife, or two bedfellows, abed in the dark

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You awake, {B}?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I am now. What is it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nothing. The roof creaks when the wind's east.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then let it creak and let me sleep.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your feet are like river stones.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then warm them. That's what you married me for.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I married you for the cow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My belly won't let me sleep.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lie on your side. It helps, a little.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. But say it helps.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Full belly, dry roof, warm bed. When did we last have all three?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hush. Don't let the luck hear you counting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you bar the door?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Twice. And the axe is under the bed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} won't come this far in.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's what {hamlet} said.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is that the beacon still lit? I can't see it from here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's lit. Go to sleep.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You didn't even look.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I don't need to look. Sleep.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I keep thinking of {dead}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So do I. Light a candle for him tomorrow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Candles cost a penny now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then light half a one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cock's crowing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cock's a liar. It's still dark.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dark or not, the field won't plough itself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The fen's singing again. Frogs and worse.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Long as it's frogs, I'll sleep.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And if it's the Crows?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then I'll wake when they knock.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cold as a clan grudge in here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Put another skin on, and stop talking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ironhand's men sleep in mail, you know.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ironhand's men don't share my blankets.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mumbling again. Something about teeth.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Was I? I dreamt the Demon King opened one eye.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Well, shut yours and keep it shut.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {steward} says the granary's low.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {steward} says lots of things at night, I'd wager.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Be serious.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'm too tired to be serious. Sleep.

who: a household at the morning table

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pass the bread.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's the heel. Mind the mould.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mould's just flavour, Mother always said.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is this all?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's water and yesterday's crust. Be glad of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'd sell my boots for an egg.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Your boots wouldn't fetch an egg.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thin porridge again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thin porridge is still porridge. Eat it before it sets.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bacon? What's the feast?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No feast. The pig died of foolishness, so we eat him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Honey on the bread. Look at us, like lords.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Enjoy it. Lords' luck never lasts the winter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eat fast. They're saying {band} hit {hamlet} last night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How many dead?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody knows yet. Eat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dates and water, same as yesterday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Water costs more than the dates now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then drink slow and chew loud.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Geoffrey Young's granary is fat, and our bowl is thin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the lord's grain, not ours.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why do we grow it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} broke a camp alone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And I say pass the salt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You don't believe it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I believe in salt.

who: family members together at home after work

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tell the one about the wolf and the miller.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Again? You know how it ends.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's why I like it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sit by me, {B}. Your hands are cold.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Been in the trough all day.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then warm them, and tell me something good.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The little one asked for supper again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What did you tell her?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That we'd eat tomorrow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we'd best find something by tomorrow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We could put by for a dowry this year.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A dowry? She's six.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And she'll be sixteen sooner than you think.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your uncle asked after {dead} again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you tell him?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I told him he's gone to {town}. He smiled.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let him keep smiling.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Hobson girl's home from the tower school.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Can she light candles with her finger?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: She can, and she's insufferable about it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why do the boys play at outlaws and heroes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They hear us talk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we'll talk quieter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Say your prayers, then bed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Brother William says the trees listen to prayers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The trees listen to everything here. Pray anyway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your grandfather held the pass with a broken spear.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You say that every night.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And every night it's still true.

who: workers and kin sharing the midday meal

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pottage again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pottage is honest food. Eat it and be quiet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You've given me more than yourself.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'm not hungry.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Liar. Split it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fine. But you're getting the burnt half.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Barley's dearer than it was at Lady Day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everything's dearer. Except us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good bread. Who baked?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Agnes. She says the oven's warmer since the new peat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mutton in the pot, ale in the jug. Who died?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody. The steward just forgot to tax us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sit in the shade, eat quick, back to the furrow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My back says otherwise.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your back can complain to the lord.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No {good} at market. None.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we'll do without, like our mothers did.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The lords signed something at the Moot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Will it put meat in this pot?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then I don't care what they signed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eel again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Eel's free. Everything else costs.

who: a household at the evening meal

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bless this food, such as it is.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Such as it is? It's good stew.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I said bless it. I didn't say it was bad.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nettle soup.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's green, it's hot, it fills the hole.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For an hour.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Save the crust for morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There'll be no crust if I'm dead of hunger by morning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You won't be. Save it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another bowl, {B}?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If I eat more I'll burst.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then burst. There's plenty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bar the shutters before we eat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In this heat?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} were at {hamlet}. Bar them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say the wells by the March taste of salt.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not ours. Drink your ale and stop fretting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Market's steadier this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we can buy cloth for the boy's breeches.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or ale.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Breeches, {A}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Saffron in the rice. The Coin's taxing it, so enjoy it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everything worth having, the Coin taxes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead} was at this table a month ago.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pour his cup anyway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Waste of good ale.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pour it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Below the salt again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Below the salt is still in the hall. Eat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord}'s in a mood. Keep your eyes on your trencher.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's he angry about?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Whatever you're about to say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Venison at the high table, gruel down here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hush. The steward has ears in the walls.

lines.text: Letters came from the Hearth-Moot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {lady} read them twice and burned one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Which one?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The one that mattered.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sir Robert drinks to the empty throne every dinner.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: To fill it or to keep it empty?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Depends who's listening.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who's that by {lady}?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A herald. Nobody important.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heralds are never nobody.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Candles are lit, so the lord means to talk late.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then I'll fill the jugs now and save my legs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} wants a hero sent at {band}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which hero?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Whichever's sober.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They kept {dead}'s seat empty.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For a week, then the dogs will have it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The clan chiefs drink from the lord's own horn tonight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then someone's being bought.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone's always being bought.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The steward wants the plate counted.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Again? We counted on Sunday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A spoon's missing. Count again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rushes need changing in the great hall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The dogs pissed in them, didn't they.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The dogs and one guest.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {steward} says half candles from now on.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Half candles, half bread, half wages.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Whole work, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sellswords in the yard. Feed them first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Before the household?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Before they decide to feed themselves.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rope's fraying.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rope's been fraying since my wedding.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the rope's lasted better than your wedding.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: First at the well again, {A}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Before the rest stir up the mud. You learn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Smell this. Does it smell of salt?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It smells of bucket.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Taste it, then.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You taste it. It's your bucket.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A penny a bucket at the spring now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Since the warlock's toll.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The warlock's gone and the price stayed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fill quick. I don't like the reeds moving.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's ducks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ducks don't wear boots.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boil it twice. Fen water's full of fever.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fuel's dearer than fever.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not when you've got it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sit down before you fall down.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'm not tired.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why are you sitting?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: An hour off our feet. The steward won't miss us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The steward misses nothing. But he naps too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lie still. Save your strength.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For whatever comes next.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lie under the hedge. Out of the sun.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's a thorn in my back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a thorn in everyone's back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Leaves are turning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then rest while you can. Harvest won't wait.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sweep the hearth, I'll shake the blankets.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You always take the outside work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because I like to hear the gossip.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why scrub the pot? There's nothing to cook in it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because if I stop scrubbing I'll start weeping.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New rushes, new candles, new shutters.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Next you'll want glass in the windows.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And why not?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Thomson boy's sweet on you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Thomson boy's sweet on everyone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not like he is on you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Moss in the thatch again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everything grows here. Even the walls.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pray it doesn't grow in the bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two families from {hamlet} in the byre.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Feed them, then set them to work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They've already offered.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where are you off to?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Chandler, cobbler, and back before the bell.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You'll never make it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Watch me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: She wants {good}, and she gave me half the coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then bargain hard.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or come home empty-handed and take the beating.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three shops for one loaf.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And it's half chaff.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The baker's giving extra to the tavern boys.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we're tavern boys today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Gate's half shut. Something about {band}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then hurry. I'm not sleeping outside the walls.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A notice on the temple door. Can you read?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Some. It says reward. And something about {player}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How much reward?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't haggle with the caravan men. They count in three tongues.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And cheat in all of them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The lord's hired swords. They're everywhere.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then mind your purse and your daughter.

who: two cooks or kin over a pot

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: More salt.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Salt's dear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bland's dearer. Nobody eats it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boil the bones a third time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's nothing left in them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's always something. Boil them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pepper! Where'd you get pepper?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A Sunward pedlar owed me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Owed you or loved you?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No {good} at any price.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we'll cook without it and swear it's better.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't use the grey salt. Throw it out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It was cheap!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's why. Throw it out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eel pie or eel stew?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Surprise me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eel pie, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oats and blood. Real highland food.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Real highland lies. Your mother put honey in it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who tracked mud on my floor?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Your husband.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then he can lick it clean.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Scrub the stair. {lady} walks it at noon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Does she look at stairs?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: She looks at everything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Blood on the bench again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Guild lads. Talked about rifts all night, then fought each other.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lye's dearer, so scrub harder.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My knuckles are already raw.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We're to wash {dead}'s room and say nothing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Say nothing about what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The library dust is older than the throne.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then it'll outlast it too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hold the lamp closer.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Any closer and I'll set your hose alight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Patch on patch on patch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's no breeches left, just patches.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Patches keep the wind out the same.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Darning by firelight. My eyes are going.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let me thread it. My eyes are younger.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And your stitches crooked.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} wears a coat older than mine.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then they need a wife or a tailor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Damp's rotted the seam again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everything rots in Reedwatch. Even oaths.

lines.speaker: A

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then you get up tomorrow and do it again.

lines.speaker: A

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: A
